title: How to set up a free zone company in the UAE
summary: Learn everything you need to know about how to set up a free zone company in the UAE. This guide covers the process and the documentation required, and how to pick the right free zone for your specific business.
body_markdown:
So, you have concluded that the best location to set up your business in the UAE is in one of the free zones, and not on the mainland. This, by far, is one of the biggest decisions you have to make to get the process of starting a company rolling.


That said, this is just the tip of the iceberg, and you will now have to decide on everything from which of the 46 free zones to choose from, to your business activity, legal structure and more before you can get your license.


This guide walks through each step so you know what to prepare, what decisions matter most and how to avoid unnecessary delays during incorporation.


## What is a free zone LLC company?


A Free Zone Limited Liability Company, FZ-LLC for short, is a type of legal entity that can be incorporated under the rules of a specific free zone authority like the[Dubai Multi Commodities Centre (DMCC)](https://dmcc.ae/) ,[Dubai International Financial Centre (DIFC)](https://www.difc.com/) , or[Abu Dhabi Global Market (ADGM)](https://www.adgm.com/) , to name a few.


It's a separate legal entity (from its shareholders), meaning it can own assets, sign contracts, and hold a bank account in its own name. There are two common structures of an FZ-LLC that depend on the number of shareholders your company has:


- **Free Zone Establishment (FZE):** If the company has only one shareholder.
- **Free Zone Company (FZ Co.):** If the company will have two or more shareholders.


You can convert an FZE to an FZ Co and vice versa later, but it will involve additional paperwork and associated expenses.


### The benefits of UAE free zone business setup


With a Free Zone LLC, you get:


- The possibility of[100% foreign ownership](https://www.moet.gov.ae/en/-/100-company-ownership) without requiring a UAE national shareholder, regardless of the free zone.
- Limited liability, i. your personal assets stay separate from the company's.
- Access to a 0% corporate tax rate on qualifying income, provided you meet Qualifying Free Zone Person conditions.
- Fast, standardised setup compared to more document-heavy structures and processes elsewhere.


## What are the prerequisites to set up a FZ-LLC?


Before you begin the process to set up a FZ-LLC, you will have to have some funds set aside and make a few critical decisions.


### Minimum registered capital


Depending on which of the 46 free zones you decide to set up your business in, you will have to set aside funds to meet the minimum share capital requirement. The amount varies per free zone. DIFC, for instance, has no minimum share capital requirement.


[According to DMCC’s schedule](https://dmcc.ae/members/support/schedule-charges) of charges, company setup package pricing varies by package and term, with published prices ranging from AED 35,484 to AED 120,000, subject to applicable fees.


### Decide on the shareholders


Depending on your chosen legal structure, your company can have one shareholder or several individual or corporate shareholders. Some legal structures also allow existing companies to become shareholders.


### Appoint a director and managers


You will also have to appoint at least one director (who has to be a person and not a corporate entity) and, if a specific zone mandates it, a manager for day-to-day operations. In some cases, this role can sometimes be held by the same person acting as director.


### Appoint a company secretary


Certain free zones also require you to hire a company secretary, while others don't. Here as well, the role can be held jointly by a director rather than needing a separate appointee.


### Choose your business activity


Every licence is linked to one or more approved business activities. Your chosen activity determines the type of licence you'll need and whether additional approvals are required from government authorities.


Once you have all of the above prerequisites addressed, you can now begin the process of setting up your business.


## The steps to registering your FZ-LLC


Once you've decided that a free zone is the right fit for your business, the registration process is fairly straightforward, with slight variation depending on the chosen free zone.


### Step 1: Choose your business activity


The first and most essential step of registering a FZ-LLC is to decide on the business activity, as it will serve as the foundation for every decision that follows. The business activity you pick will determine the type of licence you'll need and which free zones are available to you for that activity. It will also determine whether additional government approvals are required, and even the office options you can choose from.


### Step 2: Choose the right free zone


Each of the[46 free zones](https://www.uae-embassy.org/free-zones) is designed to cater to specific industries and types of businesses. Pick the free zone based on your planned business activities, budget, and whether it requires a physical office.


Here's a quick comparison of some of the UAE's most popular options.


Free Zone What is the free zone best suited for What is the free zone known for Minimum Share Capital


Dubai Multi Commodities Centre (DMCC) Trading, commodities, technology, consulting Large business ecosystem and flexible licensing AED 35,000 and upwards


Dubai International Financial Centre (DIFC) Financial services, fintech, wealth management Independent financial regulatory framework No minimum


Abu Dhabi Global Market (ADGM) Financial services, investment firms, fintech Common law framework and financial ecosystem No fixed minimum, activity-dependent


Meydan Free Zone (MFZ) Startups, consultants, e-commerce Fast digital incorporation and flexible office packages Not required to be paid up


Dubai Airport Free Zone (DAFZ) Import, export, logistics, aviation Airport connectivity and international trade Zone-dependent


Dubai World Trade Centre (DWTC) Professional services, technology, events Central Dubai location and broad licensing options Zone-dependent


### Step 3: Reserve your company's name


Once you've selected a free zone, you'll need to register your trade name. Each authority has its own naming guidelines, and the name should reflect the legal structure of your business where required.


### Step 4: Submit your application and supporting documents


After your trade name is approved, you'll be required to submit your incorporation documents. The specific list may vary from free zone to free zone, but the following are common across most free zones.


- Passport copies for shareholders and directors.
- Company incorporation documents (for corporate shareholders).
- Proposed company name.
- Application forms.
- Business plan, where required.
- Supporting resolutions or powers of attorney for certain legal structures.


### Step 5: Select your workspace


Depending on your free zone, your licence, and your business activities, you have to finalise a workspace. The options range from:


- Flexi-desks
- Co-working spaces
- Serviced offices
- Dedicated offices
- Warehouses or industrial facilities


**Pro Tip:** The option you go with will have a direct impact on your visa allocation and your future expansion options. So it's best to make this decision by taking into consideration your future business requirements.


### Step 6: Receive your licence and complete post-registration formalities


Once your application has been approved and the relevant fees have been paid, the free zone authority issues your business licence. Now, you can begin completing the remaining setup formalities like:


- Applying for residence visas where applicable.
- Opening a corporate bank account.
- Preparing your business for day-to-day operations.


Many free zones provide these services through a single point of contact.


## Compliance requirements once you're set up


Once your company is set up, you will also need to keep track of and adhere to the following requirements:


- Renewing your trade licence on time.
- [Registering for VAT](https://www.alaan.com/blog/vat-registration-uae) if your business meets the Federal Tax Authority's registration thresholds.
- [Maintaining proper accounting records per FTA to avoid penalties](https://www.alaan.com/blog/uae-corporate-tax-penalty) .
- Meeting corporate tax obligations where applicable.
- Keeping shareholder and company records up to date.


Please note that these activities will vary based on the free zone. For example, DMCC and DWTC require audited financial statements to be filed within a set period after your financial year ends. Others, like Meydan, require statements to be prepared but not necessarily filed.


## An example of setting up an FZ-LLC in Dubai


Imagine two founders looking to set up a management consultancy in Dubai. Their decision-making process and the steps they take will go something like this:


1. They will pick Management Consultancy as the primary licensed activity based on the services they plan to offer.
2. After comparing a few options, they may choose Meydan Free Zone because it supports consultancy businesses, has a straightforward incorporation process, and offers flexible workspace options.
3. Once they've agreed on a business name that complies with the authority's naming guidelines, they submit it for approval.
4. Rather than leasing a private office immediately, they opt for a flexi-desk package, which satisfies their initial operational and visa requirements while keeping setup costs down to a minimum.
5. They upload passport copies, complete the incorporation forms and submit a short business plan along with the required supporting documents.
6. Once the application is approved, the licence is issued. The founders can then apply for visas, open a corporate bank account and begin operating the business.


## Summing it up


Setting up a free zone company is one of the most straightforward ways to establish a business in the UAE, provided you make the right decisions before submitting your application. Once done, your focus should shift to two major parameters: understanding your ongoing obligations and managing your business's finances efficiently.

## FAQs


**Can I operate multiple business activities under one free zone licence?**


Many free zones allow multiple related business activities under a single licence, although the exact combination depends on the licensing authority. If your business is likely to expand into new services, it's worth checking the permitted activities before applying.


**Can a free zone company lease office space outside its free zone?**


Generally, your registered office must comply with the requirements of your chosen free zone authority. If you need a presence elsewhere, the available options depend on your business activity and the regulations of both jurisdictions.


**How long does it actually take to set up an FZ-LLC?**


For a standard, non-regulated activity with documentation in order, licensing can often be completed within a few working days. Regulated activities, financial services in particular, take longer due to additional approvals.
